papers.title: Isoflurane anesthesia CNS recovery state: ultra-slow oscillations and cellular-stress-responsive gene expression
papers.summary: Compared recovery from 4 h isoflurane anesthesia with time-matched sleep and sleep deprivation in male C57BL/6J mice using EEG/EMG and frontal cortex RNA sequencing; isoflurane recovery produced rebound arousal, fragmented NREM, and persistent ultra-slow EEG oscillations normalizing within two weeks. Transcriptomics showed isoflurane and sleep deprivation induced largely distinct cortical programs, with isoflurane enriching integrated stress response and unfolded protein response genes while sleep deprivation showed an mTOR-associated growth-permissive profile.

papers.title: Firing Without Wiring: How REM-like Sleep Reactivation Rebalances Excitation and Inhibition to Orthogonalize Memories
papers.summary: Using recurrent neural networks trained with Equilibrium Propagation, the study shows that REM-like sleep reduces memory interference by decorrelating task-specific neuronal populations through a mechanism termed reactivation-targeted pruning, where plasticity is confined to the most recently activated population and depressive excitatory input from older-memory populations. This mechanism held under Dale's law and required only excitatory synaptic depression, without inhibitory plasticity.

papers.title: Zona incerta circuits in cognition and the regulation of sleep and wakefulness: potential relevance to Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: Reviews evidence that the heterogeneous zona incerta (ZI) contains distinct cell populations and projections supporting memory, novelty seeking, cortical plasticity, sleep promotion, REM sleep, wake transitions, and sleep homeostasis, framing it as a state-dependent subcortical regulatory platform. Proposes two testable models for ZI involvement in Alzheimer's disease phenotypes, noting that direct human causal evidence is lacking.

papers.title: Correction: Cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (CIRBP) adjusts clock-gene expression and REM-sleep recovery following sleep deprivation.
papers.summary: Published erratum correcting the eLife article on cold-inducible RNA-binding protein (CIRBP) regulation of clock-gene expression and REM-sleep recovery after sleep deprivation; no abstract or findings are supplied.

papers.title: Layer 1 NDNF interneurons form distinct subpopulations with opposite activation patterns during sleep in freely behaving mice
papers.summary: Used simultaneous cell-specific calcium imaging and local field potential recordings in freely moving mice to examine layer 1 NDNF interneurons during NREM sleep, finding three distinct populations with stage-tuned activity. REM-active L1 NDNF cells inhibited the network at sharp-wave ripple onset depending on spindle coupling, largely via GABAB receptors, suggesting a role in gating SWR-spindle information transfer.

papers.title: Behavioral, Transcriptomic, and Neuroinflammatory Effects of Sleep Deprivation: Insights From Separate Acute and Chronic Experimental Paradigms.
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6J mice, acute 6-h sleep deprivation alleviated despair-like behavior in a pain-depression model while chronic 14-day sleep deprivation induced anxiety- and despair-like behavior. Transcriptomic profiling of five cortical regions implicated the prefrontal cortex (notably Plin4 and Sult1a1), and multiple inflammatory cytokines decreased after acute but increased after chronic sleep deprivation.

papers.title: EEG Pathology Detection via Clinical Concept Bottleneck Models
papers.summary: Introduces concept bottleneck models (CBMs) for EEG pathology detection that use clinical EEG biomarkers as an interpretable bottleneck, comparing black-box, hybrid CBM, and pure CBM variants on TUAB and CAUEEG datasets. CBMs approach baseline accuracy on TUAB (82.7-82.9% vs 83.6%) but are 2-5 percentage points lower on CAUEEG; pure CBM shows concept fidelity issues that are mitigated by increasing concept loss weight at some accuracy cost.

papers.title: Phasic pupil responses to melanopsin- and cone-directed stimulation remain stable across circadian time
papers.summary: Using a 40-hour ultra-short sleep-wake protocol with silent-substitution pupillometry in healthy adults, the authors tested whether phasic pupil responses to melanopsin- and cone-directed stimuli vary with circadian phase. Hierarchical cosinor comparisons favored constant-level over circadian models for phasic amplitude across all five stimulus conditions, not supporting circadian modulation under the tested parameters.

papers.title: Sleep-state transition instability with recurrent multisystem activation: A case-based phenotypic framework.
papers.summary: Describes eight cases of recurrent motor activation centered on sleep onset or early sleep-state transitions with variable sensory, autonomic, and other non-motor symptoms, and proposes the provisional phenotype SSTI-RMA as a hypothesis-generating descriptive construct rather than an established diagnosis. No validated polysomnographic signature, biomarker, or prevalence estimate currently exists for this phenotype.

papers.title: Sleep underestimation and subjective sleep appraisal: Limited value of routine polysomnographic and electroencephalographic features.
papers.summary: In 225 adults undergoing in-laboratory polysomnography, self-rated sleep quality was more consistently associated with sleep underestimation than routine PSG or EEG features, and none of 600 EEG features survived FDR correction. An EEG-enhanced model did not improve out-of-fold discrimination over a three-predictor clinical baseline (AUC 0.6564 vs 0.6786).

papers.title: Sleep Stage Classification Across Heterogeneous EEG/EOG Channels with Multi-channel Differential Transformer.
papers.summary: Proposes SleepDIFFormer, a multi-channel differential transformer framework with cross-domain alignment for heterogeneous EEG/EOG representation learning, trained across multiple sleep-staging datasets as source domains. It achieved superior performance versus existing approaches on five datasets under domain generalization settings, with ablation and attention-weight analyses supporting its discriminative representations.

papers.title: REM Atonia Index Cutoffs for REM Sleep Without Atonia: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis of Adult Diagnostic Performance.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 30 studies found that chin-EMG REM Atonia Index discriminates established REM sleep behavior disorder with pooled sensitivity 0.850 and specificity 0.895, and RAI was lower in RBD by a pooled mean difference of -0.263. However, heterogeneous thresholds (0.80-0.90) and sparse normative data argue against a universal numerical cutoff, supporting continuous reporting of RAI with age-conditioned interpretation.

papers.title: Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome: Unloading the Respiratory System with Expiratory Pressure.
papers.summary: This perspective proposes that abdominal obesity-induced reductions in expiratory reserve volume, functional residual capacity, and end-expiratory lung volume are upstream mechanical abnormalities linking OSA, increased work of breathing, sleep hypoventilation, and daytime hypercapnia in obesity hypoventilation syndrome. Within this framework, CPAP and expiratory positive airway pressure act partly by mechanical unloading through raising end-expiratory lung volume, with weight loss as structural unloading.

papers.title: Nonlinear Feature Modeling Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks in Electroencephalography for Depression Classification: Deep Learning Study.
papers.summary: The authors introduced Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-based convolutional architectures (ConvKAN and ConvKAN Efficient) for EEG-based depression classification on the EDRA dataset. ConvKAN Efficient achieved the best performance, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score all exceeding 94%, outperforming conventional CNN and traditional machine learning approaches.

papers.title: Single-Lead EEG-based virtual reality motion sickness detection using interpretable feature selection.
papers.summary: Proposes a SHAP-based single-lead EEG modeling and feature-screening framework for lightweight VRMS detection, selecting FT11 as the optimal lead and achieving 87.53% ± 0.73% accuracy with seven features under window-level tenfold cross-validation. A post hoc LOSO test showed limited cross-subject generalization, which the authors caution is not a fully independent estimate.

papers.title: Astrocyte molecular rhythm disruption in nucleus accumbens promotes increased binge-like drinking in mice.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Used AAV8-Gfap-Cre to ablate molecular rhythms in nucleus accumbens astrocytes of BMAL1-floxed mice, finding increased binge-like drinking in drinking-in-the-light and drinking-in-the-dark paradigms (d = 1.44) without changes in other drinking paradigms or behaviors. Identifies a role for NAc astrocyte rhythmicity in temporal organization of reward circuitry and binge-drinking susceptibility.

papers.title: Circadian rhythms and sleep disturbances: a conceptual perspective with implications for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.
papers.summary: Conceptual review of how circadian rhythm and sleep disturbances may influence autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease progression, linking circadian disruption to sympathetic activation, RAAS dysregulation, elevated vasopressin, mTOR activation, and impaired fatty acid oxidation. Discusses chronotherapy and sleep hygiene interventions, including timed antihypertensives, diuretics, tolvaptan, melatonin, and light exposure, as adjunctive strategies.

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity of resting EEG in people exposed to armed conflict and controls
papers.summary: Compared resting-state EEG spectral power and functional connectivity in 122 Colombian adults (74 exposed to armed conflict, 48 controls) across 78 corrected contrasts. No spectral power or regional connectivity contrast remained significant after multiple testing correction, though median occipital and global alpha power was lower in exposed participants with broad confidence intervals.

papers.title: A Humanized Mouse Model of DRPLA Recapitulates Epilepsy and Demonstrates Antisense Oligonucleotide-Mediated Disease Modification
papers.summary: Characterized a fully humanized ATN1 mouse model expressing mutant atrophin-1 with 112 CAG repeats, showing increased seizure susceptibility, spontaneous behavioral seizures on video-EEG, ataxia, and early death. Antisense oligonucleotide treatment normalized seizure threshold, reduced ataxia, protected against early death, and eliminated spontaneous seizures, supporting ATN1 as an epilepsy-related risk factor.

papers.title: De-escalating Therapy in Obstructive Sleep Apnoea After Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonist-Induced Weight Loss: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on weight change and OSA severity, incretin (GLP-1 and dual agonist) efficacy in OSA, and PAP withdrawal studies, noting consistent AHI, weight, and blood pressure reductions but unresolved questions about weight mediation, cardiovascular risk reduction, and true remission, and proposes a structured reversible framework for therapy de-escalation.

papers.title: Composite sleep patterns and the allergy-related composite outcome among American and Chinese older adults: exploration of depressive symptoms as a potential mediator.
papers.journal: The Journal of asthma : official journal of the Association for the Care of Asthma
papers.summary: In NHANES 2005-2006 older adults, poor versus healthy composite sleep was associated with higher odds of an allergy-related composite outcome (OR 2.100), wheeze, and sneeze, with depressive symptoms accounting for an estimated 22.5% of the total association; CHARLS longitudinal analysis linked impaired sleep quality to incident asthma (OR 1.689) with 28.3% mediated through depressive symptoms.

papers.title: The impact of creatine on brain functions.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes evidence that creatine supplementation can raise brain creatine and may benefit cognition under high metabolic demand (e.g., stress, sleep deprivation) and augment mood disorder treatment, possibly via mTORC1, while evidence on generalized fatigue remains ambiguous and findings are limited by methodological heterogeneity.

papers.title: Prebiotics in sport and exercise: current evidence, practical applications, and methodological considerations.
papers.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
papers.summary: Narrative review of prebiotic intake in athletic populations, reporting evidence that prebiotics may improve gut barrier integrity, reduce exercise-associated gastrointestinal symptoms, increase salivary IgA secretion rate, and reduce duration/severity of upper respiratory symptoms in trained individuals. It highlights limited high-quality evidence and calls for adequately powered studies with microbiome/metabolome profiling and robust performance measures.

papers.title: Responses to unannounced rule changes in adults with developmental disabilities: A community-based pilot study with consumer-grade EEG
papers.summary: A community-based pilot study recorded resting-state EEG with a 14-channel wireless system and administered a probabilistic reversal learning task in 12 adults with developmental disabilities at a day-service center. Flatter frontal aperiodic spectra were associated with fewer switches after negative feedback (ρ = .80) and more perseverative errors (ρ = -.72), and frontal alpha peak amplitude correlated with accuracy (ρ = .77), suggesting field EEG can capture individual differences in responses to unannounced rule changes.

papers.title: The qualitative exploration of work productivity among chronic rhinitis patients.
papers.summary: Qualitative study combining a literature review with semi-structured interviews of 19 chronic rhinitis patients, using thematic analysis to identify eight themes describing reduced work productivity, including absenteeism, presenteeism, reduced efficiency, sleepiness at work, and workplace stigma. The findings are framed as informing targeted management strategies.

papers.title: [The association between circadian rhythm disruption-related behaviors and myopia in children and adolescents].
papers.journal: Zhonghua yu fang yi xue za zhi [Chinese journal of preventive medicine]
papers.summary: This review systematically examines associations between circadian rhythm-disrupting behaviors—irregular sleep, social jetlag, and nighttime blue-light exposure—and the onset and progression of myopia in children and adolescents, along with potential pathogenic mechanisms. It also summarizes myopia interventions targeting circadian behavioral abnormalities to inform precise prevention and control.

papers.title: A novel age-based physiological definition of adherence to pediatric long-term non-invasive ventilation: an exploratory study.
papers.summary: This retrospective cross-sectional study proposed a novel age-based physiological definition of adherence to pediatric long-term non-invasive ventilation (≥70% of age-specific minimum recommended sleep duration on ≥70% of nights) and found it yielded lower adherence rates (66.25%) than adult-derived definitions (78.75% and 83.75%), suggesting adult thresholds overestimate adherence in children.

papers.title: Gut microbiome composition and cardiometabolic risk among healthcare workers: findings from the EXPONIT study.
papers.journal: Nutrition, metabolism, and cardiovascular diseases : NMCD
papers.summary: In the EXPONIT study, 16S rRNA sequencing of fecal samples from healthcare workers was used to test associations between gut microbiome diversity and composition and cardiometabolic outcomes, with exploration of interactions by shift work, sleep quality, and chronotype. Beta diversity was associated with excess body weight (PERMANOVA p = 0.01, R2 = 0.7%), and specific genera (Lachnospiraceae-unclassified-genus-008, Escherichia/Shigella, Alistipes) were linked to BMI or waist-to-hip ratio, while no associations were found with metabolic biomarkers.

papers.title: A Reproducible Safety Assessment Model for Concurrent Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation with Implanted Intracranial Electroencephalography Electrodes.
papers.summary: Developed and validated a reproducible agarose-phantom framework for assessing TMS safety with implanted sEEG electrodes, quantifying displacement, heating, and induced currents. Across single-pulse, repetitive (1-50 Hz), and theta-burst TMS, sEEG lead displacement stayed micrometer-scale (max 1-s mean 16.27 μm), temperature increases remained within the 2°C threshold (max 0.073°C), and induced voltages and charge densities stayed below safety limits.

papers.title: Differential Cerebral Perfusion Patterns Across Migraine Phenotypes: An Exploratory ASL MRI Study.
papers.summary: Characterized cerebral blood flow alterations across migraine phenotypes using 3D pseudo-continuous ASL MRI in 143 migraine patients and 49 controls. Migraine with aura showed increased nCBF in a right cerebellar-occipitotemporal cluster (surviving covariate adjustment) versus migraine without aura, and a combined clinical-imaging model showed higher apparent AUC than clinical alone.

papers.title: Enhancement of gut-microbiome-based classification of prodromal Parkinson's Disease cases by hyperparameter tuning, integration of multimodal data, and meta-analysis.
papers.summary: This study classified prodromal Parkinson's disease (RBD cases versus controls) from public gut microbiome datasets using batch correction, hyperparameter tuning, multimodal feature integration, and meta-analysis, identifying six depleted short-chain fatty acid-producing genera shared by RBD and PD groups. The tuned model reached an AUC of 0.889, rising to a peak mean AUC of 0.917 when microbial and clinical features were combined, while the six SCFA-producing taxa alone retained a mean AUC of 0.853.

papers.title: Effects of an Esketamine-Containing Induction Regimen on Postoperative Sleep, Analgesia, and Postpartum Depression in Parturients with Sleep Disorders Undergoing Cesarean Section Under General Anesthesia: A Double-Blind Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: In a double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial of 90 parturients with preoperative sleep disorders undergoing cesarean section under general anesthesia, an esketamine-containing induction regimen (esketamine 0.25 mg/kg plus propofol 1.0 mg/kg versus saline plus propofol 2.0 mg/kg) significantly improved the primary outcome of sleep NRS on postoperative day 1 (mean difference 3.0, 95% CI 2.0–4.0, P<0.001). Secondary exploratory outcomes suggested early pain benefits and lower continuous EPDS scores on POD 3, but the trial was not powered for secondary or safety outcomes and differing propofol doses prevent isolation of esketamine's specific effect.

papers.title: Effect of a Subanesthetic Dose of Esketamine on Postoperative Sleep Disturbance After Oocyte Retrieval Under Intravenous Anesthesia: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: In a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial of 196 women undergoing oocyte retrieval under intravenous anesthesia, a single subanesthetic dose of esketamine 0.2 mg/kg reduced the estimated incidence of postoperative sleep disturbance on POD 3 versus saline (13.06% vs 24.90%; RR 0.52, 95% CI 0.28–0.99; P=0.047), with similar per-protocol results. Postoperative pain at 30 minutes was lower with esketamine, but dreaming was more frequent and time to full alertness and PACU stay were modestly longer.

papers.title: Acute Psychosis and Dissociative Syndrome Following Binge Recreational Nitrous Oxide Use: A Case Report.
papers.summary: Reports a case in a female in her early 20s who developed acute psychotic and dissociative symptoms over three days after binge recreational nitrous oxide and MDMA use with sleep deprivation, with elevated homocysteine and low-normal B12 indicating functional cobalamin deficiency. Risperidone was followed by neutropenia that resolved after switching to aripiprazole, and the patient recovered by day 12 with no psychotic symptoms at three weeks.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine for Depression With Anxiety and Somatic Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
keywords: integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine
papers.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials found that integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine reduced depression severity (MD -3.95, 95% CI -4.71 to -3.19) and anxiety symptoms (MD -3.95, 95% CI -4.65 to -3.26) versus control interventions, with generally good tolerability but low certainty of evidence.

papers.title: Interplay of action-based prediction and top-down attention: EEG evidence for joint modulation of late perceptual processing.
papers.summary: An EEG study in which participants viewed sequential gratings that were predicted/self-generated or unpredicted/externally generated and attended or not found no modulation of early visual potentials (N1a), but P3b amplitude was reduced for predicted task-relevant stimuli and prediction-related P3b latency differences correlated with faster reaction times. Multivariate, time-frequency, and behavioral analyses suggested that top-down attention and action-based prediction jointly facilitate late perceptual and decision-related processing.

papers.title: Cannabidiol (CBD) for Pain: A Narrative Review of Evidence to Date.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesized preclinical, pharmacokinetic, and clinical evidence on cannabidiol for pain, finding strong biological plausibility but inconsistent clinical translation. High-quality trials in knee osteoarthritis, fibromyalgia, and acute low back pain failed to separate CBD from placebo, and dose-dependent hepatotoxicity risk was noted.

papers.title: Ayurveda in Integrative Oncology: Aligning Traditional Principles with Conventional Cancer Care.
papers.summary: This review examines how Ayurveda can be incorporated into integrative oncology across the cancer care continuum, comparing and contrasting Ayurvedic and integrative oncology approaches to nutrition, exercise, mind-body practices, sleep, and herbal supplements. It argues for a patient-centered, evidence-informed integrative model and aims to stimulate multidisciplinary collaboration and further research between oncology providers and Ayurveda clinicians.

papers.title: Early Postoperative Psychological Resilience Patterns and Associated Factors in Patients with Knee Stiffness Undergoing Arthroscopic Release Surgery: A Latent Class Growth Model Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 240 patients undergoing arthroscopic release for knee stiffness, latent class growth modeling identified three early postoperative psychological resilience trajectories (Low Declining 17.1%, Moderate Stable 68.8%, High Increasing 14.2%); lower perceived social support and poorer sleep quality were associated with the Low Declining group, and lower education, lower social support, and lower ERRI scores with the Moderate Stable group.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of pain experience and quality of life in patients with oral lichen planus and burning mouth syndrome.
papers.journal: Journal of oral & facial pain and headache
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional comparison of 46 patients with oral lichen planus and 50 with burning mouth syndrome, burning mouth syndrome showed higher pain intensity and catastrophizing, whereas oral lichen planus showed greater mastication-related pain interference and poorer quality of life; regression identified mastication and rumination as predictors in OLP and sleep disturbance, rumination, and magnification in BMS.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
